content: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and octreotide both prolong the QTc interval. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and olanzapine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the plasma levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. If adverse effects occur, further reduce the dose to 50 mg/day. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Avoid in patients with congenital long QT syndrome, and consider ECG monitoring in patients with concomitant QT-prolonging medications, electrolyte abnormalities, congestive heart failure, or bradyarrhythmias. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of osimertinib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no alternative exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and oxaliplatin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and panobinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Panobinostat significantly prolongs the QT interval, and its prescribing information advises against use with other QT-prolonging drugs. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pemigatinib dose may be resumed. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and perphenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of phenindione by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of pitavastatin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Additionally, erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the risk of pitavastatin toxicity, potentially leading to myopathy due to OATP1B1 inhibition. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and pitolisant both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of pomalidomide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of prednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of prednisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, prednisone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and pretomanid both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity, and alcohol or other hepatotoxic agents should be avoided. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and primaquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and prochlorperazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and promazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and promethazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the effects of protamine by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and protriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of quetiapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of prolonged QTc interval. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of resmetirom by mechanisms involving OATP1B1/3 transport inhibition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of revefenacin by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters, which may increase systemic exposure to its active metabolite. Coadministration is not recommended. Ribociclib increases the toxicity of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of rifabutin by decreasing its metabolism. Conversely, rifabutin decreases the levels of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of riociguat by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If used, monitor for signs of hypotension and adjust the dose as needed. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, ritonavir increases the levels of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the previous selumetinib dose. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and sertraline both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and sevoflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Additionally, siponimod and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, solifenacin and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Sotorasib decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information of the P-gp substrate for dosage modifications. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of sulbactam/durlobactam by mechanisms involving OATP1 transport inhibition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, sunitinib and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, tacrolimus and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If used, limit tadalafil to 5 mg/day for daily use or 10 mg every 72 hours for as-needed use. Avoid concurrent use of tadalafil for pulmonary hypertension in patients taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the tazemetostat dose as per the drug monograph. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended in its product labeling. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and tetrabenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of theophylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and thioridazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug.
